sentences: Local certification gives each graph vertex a certificate that it verifies using only its nearby information.
The source asks whether a hereditary graph class can require certificates of size growing faster than linearly in the number of vertices.
It also asks for this phenomenon under the stronger requirement of closure under subgraphs.
Existing linear lower bounds motivate seeking a larger information barrier.
Such examples would show that even deletion-stable structural properties can demand exceptionally large local evidence for a globally correct decision.
